headline: Strategist Jim Bianco calculates that AI-related stocks would make up 51% of the S&P 500 if SpaceX were already in the index.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: a clear measure of how concentrated the market has become; facts support the headline, but it is a hypothetical.
importance_line: What changed is a number showing how much of the US stock index one theme could fill, which matters first to savers whose index funds and pensions track it, then to fund managers, and the doubt is that it is one strategist's what-if, since SpaceX cannot join before June 2027.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Jim Bianco of Bianco Research calculated, in a post on X, that AI-related stocks would be 51% of the S&P 500 if SpaceX were in it, and 55% if Anthropic and OpenAI also listed, though S&P rules mean SpaceX cannot join before June 2027. Bianco noted that the last time one theme passed 50% of the index was the railroads in the 19th century, and Bank of America strategists say 10 AI stocks now make up 42% of US market value, against about 40% at the peak of most past bubbles and 63% in the railroad boom.
notes: Read the original page in full. The Bank of America figure is relayed by Yahoo Finance, not read at the source.
